key_insight: Instead of optimizing memory summaries only for final task success, the paper trains them to preserve a clear internal belief about the latent task state by minimizing belief entropy.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to make long-horizon LLM agents more reliable by improving intermediate memory quality, reducing drift, and preserving useful context at very large token scales.
method: Defines Belief Entropy as a self-supervised proxy for how uncertain the model is about the hidden task state from its current memory.
Introduces Metacognitive Memory Policy Optimization (MMPO), which penalizes memory summaries that induce high epistemic uncertainty.
Provides fine-grained supervision at the memory level rather than relying only on sparse outcome-based reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MMPO outperforms prior methods on diverse long-horizon tasks and retains 97.1% performance even at 1.75M-token contexts.
watch_item: Belief entropy is only a proxy for latent-state clarity, so its effectiveness may depend on how well the proxy aligns with the true task state and on the cost of computing it at scale.
paper_title: Meta-Cognitive Memory Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
